company: Stockland (Stockland Corporation Limited and Stockland Trust Management Limited as responsible entity for Stockland Trust)
title: Security Trading Policy (Version 1.1)
date_next_review: When there are relevant changes in business practice, legislation or compliance obligations, and at least every two years

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: All Stockland employees, including permanent, casual and fixed term employees and temporary workers, and non-executive Directors, of Stockland Corporation Limited and its related companies and trusts. All the substantive prohibitions in section 5.3 and 5.4 (derivatives, security interests, margin lending, short selling, short-term trading) apply to this tier without differentiation.

tiers.name: non-executive Directors
tiers.description: Non-executive Directors of Stockland and SCPL. Within the defined term Employees but distinguished by needing the Chairperson's prior written consent to Deal even in a Permitted Trading Window, by the minimum securityholding of 100% of annual fees within three years of joining the Board, and by the obligation to inform the Company Secretary within three business days after a Disclosure Date.

tiers.name: Managing Director
tiers.description: The Managing Director of Stockland. Requires prior written consent to Deal in any Permitted Trading Window and is subject to a disposal floor of two times Fixed Pay on Securities acquired under equity-based plans granted on or after 1 July 2010. Section 5.1(b) does not expressly name a Consent Authority for the Managing Director's own dealings.

tiers.name: Senior Executives
tiers.description: Employees who from time to time report directly to the Managing Director. Require the Chairperson's prior written consent to Deal even in a Permitted Trading Window and are subject to a disposal floor of one times Fixed Pay on Securities acquired under equity-based plans granted on or after 1 July 2010.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: Persons and entities closely connected to a Director or Employee, including a spouse, domestic partner, child or dependent, a spouse's or domestic partner's child or dependent, a company controlled by the Director or Employee, and any other closely related party as defined in the Corporations Act. Employees must ensure their Associates do not trade other than in accordance with the Policy and must deal with the Consent Authority on their behalf.

definitions.hedging_definition: Derivatives means any option, hedge, derivative or like instrument which limits exposure to the market price of Securities whether now or in the future.

windows.start_anchor: the first trading day after the day that Stockland's full year results are announced to ASX (usually in August)
windows.end_anchor: six weeks later, closing at 4pm AEST

windows.start_anchor: the first trading day after the day that Stockland's half year results are announced to ASX (usually in February)
windows.end_anchor: six weeks later, closing at 4pm AEST

windows.start_anchor: the first trading day after the day that Stockland's Annual General Meetings are held (usually in October)
windows.end_anchor: six weeks later, closing at 4pm AEST

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Chairperson may at any time, by written notification to Employees, impose an additional period during which Employees or a specific group are prohibited from Dealing while Stockland is considering matters subject to Listing Rule 3.1A. The additional period may be temporary or permanent, and those notified must keep the notification confidential. An application for consent to sell in Exceptional Circumstances remains available.

rules.detail: Absolute, permanent ban on dealing in Derivatives over Securities by every Employee, including non-executive Directors, the Managing Director and Senior Executives, and their Associates. There is no vesting-state qualification, no venue limit, no consent route and no exemption; the Exceptional Circumstances relief in section 5.1 is confined to selling or disposing of Securities.
rules.evidence: Employees must not Deal in Derivatives over Securities at any time.

rules.detail: The defined term Derivatives is an effects-based hedging definition: any option, hedge, derivative or like instrument which limits exposure to the market price of Securities, now or in the future. Both legs of a collar and the collar as a whole fall within it, so hedging of vested, unrestricted Stockland securities is banned outright.
rules.evidence: Derivatives means any option, hedge, derivative or like instrument which limits exposure to the market price of Securities whether now or in the future.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named, but any prepaid forward, structured product or similar is a 'like instrument which limits exposure to the market price of Securities' and is banned by section 5.3(a), and any monetisation that gives the financier recourse to the Securities is banned by the Security Interest prohibition in section 5.3(b).
rules.evidence: Employees must not enter into any margin lending arrangements or create or give a mortgage, or security or other right to a lender or financier ("Security Interest") over any Securities.

rules.detail: Flat ban on short selling Securities by all Employees. The term is not defined, so the ordinary meaning applies.

Securities lending is not named. Deal is defined only as directly or indirectly acquiring or disposing of Securities. A stock loan to a financier would in any event be caught by the ban on giving 'security or other right to a lender or financier' over Securities.

Contracts for difference are not named but are a derivative or like instrument limiting exposure to the market price of Securities, so they fall inside the defined term Derivatives and within the absolute ban. A short CFD would separately breach the short selling prohibition.
rules.evidence: Employees must not Deal in Derivatives over Securities at any time.

rules.detail: All Employees, including non-executive Directors, and their Associates are banned from entering any margin lending arrangement. Only Security Interests existing before the Policy was approved are grandfathered.
rules.evidence: Employees must not enter into any margin lending arrangements or create or give a mortgage, or security or other right to a lender or financier ("Security Interest") over any Securities.

rules.detail: Creating or giving a mortgage, security or any other right to a lender or financier over any Securities is prohibited. The definition of Security Interest is deliberately wide, reaching not only formal security but 'other right' given to a lender or financier. Pre-existing Security Interests are excluded from the Policy's operation.
rules.evidence: create or give a mortgage, or security or other right to a lender or financier ("Security Interest") over any Securities. Any Security Interest existing prior to the date this Policy is approved is excluded from the operation of this Policy.

rules.detail: The prohibition is not confined to margin loans; it captures any arrangement under which a lender or financier is given a mortgage, security or other right over Stockland Securities, whatever the loan-to-value ratio or purpose. There is no approval route and no waiver power for it.
rules.evidence: Employees must not enter into any margin lending arrangements or create or give a mortgage, or security or other right to a lender or financier ("Security Interest") over any Securities.

rules.detail: Consent will generally not be given for short-term trading, defined as buying and selling Securities within a six month period. Expressed as a consent policy rather than an absolute ban, but for Employees who need no consent in a Permitted Trading Window it operates as a statement of expectation that they be long-term investors.
rules.evidence: Consent under section 5.1 will generally not be given to allow an Employee to engage in short-term trading of Securities. An Employee would be engaging in short-term trading of Securities if they were to buy and sell Securities within a six (6) month period.

clearance.evidence: the Managing Director, non-executive Directors and Senior Executives may Deal in Securities during a: A. Permitted Trading Window, after first obtaining on a confidential basis the written consent of the Consent Authority

clearance.approver: Not expressly assigned: section 5.1(b) names the Chairperson only for non-executive Directors and Senior Executives, and the Managing Director, Chief Financial Officer or a delegated executive for all other Employees
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within three business days after a Disclosure Date
clearance.evidence: the Managing Director, non-executive Directors and Senior Executives may Deal in Securities during a: A. Permitted Trading Window, after first obtaining on a confidential basis the written consent of the Consent Authority

clearance.approver: For dealings in a Prohibited Period only: the Managing Director, Chief Financial Officer or another executive delegated by the Managing Director
clearance.evidence: Employees (other than the Managing Director, non-executive Directors and Senior Executives) may Deal in Securities during a: A. Permitted Trading Window without obtaining prior written clearance;

clearance.approver: The Consent Authority applicable to the related Employee, who must communicate with the Consent Authority on the Associate's behalf

exceptions.approver: Consent Authority (Chairperson for non-executive Directors and Senior Executives; Managing Director, CFO or delegate for other Employees; Chairperson of the People and Culture Committee for the Chairperson)
exceptions.evidence: the Director, Senior Executive or Employee is suffering severe financial hardship where he or she has a pressing financial commitment that cannot be reasonably satisfied other than by selling the Securities;
there is a requirement to sell the Securities under a court order or court enforceable undertaking or other legal or regulatory requirement;

there are other exceptional circumstances for which the sale of the Securities is the only reasonable course of action available, for example to comply with a Court Order or a bona fide family dispute.
Any Security Interest existing prior to the date this Policy is approved is excluded from the operation of this Policy.
transfers of Securities from one broker account to another, provided there is no change in the beneficial interest in the Securities at the time of the transfer;

investments in, or trading in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in Securities and including an exchange-traded index fund) that happens to hold Securities and where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of an independent third party;
a disposal of Securities arising from the acceptance of a takeover offer, a scheme of arrangement or equal access buy-back or capital reduction;
an acquisition of Securities under any distribution and dividend reinvestment plan or security purchase plan made available to all or most of the securityholders
applications for, and acquisitions under those applications of, Securities under any employee security plan but not any subsequent Dealing in those Securities;

exceptions.approver: Prior written clearance in accordance with the Policy
exceptions.evidence: dealings under a non-discretionary trading plan for which prior written clearance has been provided in accordance with procedures set out in this Policy
transfers of Securities to a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which prior written clearance has been provided in accordance with section 5.1 of this Policy;

financing.minimum_shareholding_requirement: Yes, twice over. Non-Executive Directors must acquire and hold a minimum securityholding equivalent to 100% of their annual Non-Executive Director's fee within three years of joining the Board. The Managing Director and Senior Executives may not dispose of Securities acquired from awards under Stockland equity-based plans granted on or after 1 July 2010 unless immediately after the disposal they would still hold Securities worth two times Fixed Pay (Managing Director) or one times Fixed Pay (other Senior Executives), with a carve-out for sales reasonably necessary to pay tax on vesting under a long term incentive plan. The Policy does not say whether hedged or encumbered Securities are excluded from the count, but hedging and encumbrance are prohibited in any event.

external_documents: Continuous Disclosure and External Communications Policy
exemption_authority: The Consent Authority may consent to Dealing in a Prohibited Period only where Exceptional Circumstances exist (severe financial hardship with a pressing financial commitment, a court order, court enforceable undertaking or other legal or regulatory requirement, or other exceptional circumstances where sale is the only reasonable course of action). The relief is expressed in terms of selling Securities and does not extend to the section 5.3 prohibitions on Derivatives and Security Interests, which have no waiver mechanism. Consent will not be given if there is any possibility that the Policy could be breached, no reasons are given, the decision is final and binding, and a refusal must be kept confidential.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Employees must not Deal in Derivatives over Securities at any time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Both legs of the collar are prohibited for everyone the Policy covers, at every vesting state, with no consent route and no waiver, so the structure fails before the financing is even considered.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Derivatives means any option, hedge, derivative or like instrument which limits exposure to the market price of Securities whether now or in the future.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The definition turns on economic effect rather than instrument type, so a cash-settled, synthetic or forward-starting structure is caught just as squarely as a physically settled put and call.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Employees must not enter into any margin lending arrangements or create or give a mortgage, or security or other right to a lender or financier ("Security Interest") over any Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg is separately prohibited, and the words 'or other right to a lender or financier' are wide enough to catch even a negative pledge or a call option written in favour of the financing bank.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any Security Interest existing prior to the date this Policy is approved is excluded from the operation of this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The only permitted encumbrances are those predating the Policy's approval in May 2025, so no new facility can be granted and the exclusion cannot be extended to a refinancing or an increase.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Exceptional Circumstances means where: (a) the Director, Senior Executive or Employee is suffering severe financial hardship ... (c) there are other exceptional circumstances for which the sale of the Securities is the only reasonable course of action available.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Every limb of the exceptional circumstances relief is framed around selling Securities, so there is no route to a hedged or financed position even in hardship; the only sanctioned answer to a liquidity need is an outright sale with consent.

bespoke_clauses.topic: settlement must complete inside the window
bespoke_clauses.clause: A Deal or Dealing in Securities will be within a Permitted Trading Window if the trade has been settled and completed before the closure of the Permitted Trading Window. ... If the transaction has not been completed or settled before the closure of the Permitted Trading Window at 4pm (AEST) on that day ... the Employee must cancel the trade.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unusually strict: settlement, not execution, must fall inside the window, so any physically settled leg would need to complete well before the window closes.

bespoke_clauses.clause: These executives are prohibited from disposing of Securities acquired from awards under any Stockland equity-based plans granted on or after 1 July 2010, unless immediately after that disposal they would continue to hold a minimum number of Securities with a value being the equivalent of two times Fixed Pay for the Managing Director and one times Fixed Pay for all other Senior Executives.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even an outright sale, the only permitted form of monetisation, is floored at two times Fixed Pay for the Managing Director and one times for other Senior Executives.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Consent will not be given under section 5.1 if there is any possibility that this Policy could be breached. No reason will be given for the grant or refusal of consent to Deal in Securities. The decision to refuse consent is final and binding on the person seeking consent.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The 'any possibility' standard means a Consent Authority could not approve any transaction with a bank that touches the derivative or security interest prohibitions, and there is no appeal.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Chairperson may, at any time, through written notification to Employees impose an additional period for which Employees (or a specific group) are prohibited from Dealing in Securities while Stockland is considering matters subject to Listing Rule 3.1A. This additional period may be temporary or permanent.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A blackout can be imposed indefinitely and must be kept confidential, so even a permitted sale can become impossible without the executive being able to explain why.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Associate means persons and entities closely connected to a Director or Employee and includes a spouse, domestic partner, child or dependent ... company controlled by the Director or Employee and any other closely related party, as defined in the Corporations Act.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar or the loan through a spouse, family company or other closely related party does not avoid either prohibition.

bespoke_clauses.clause: dealings under a non-discretionary trading plan for which prior written clearance has been provided in accordance with procedures set out in this Policy and where: the Director or Employee did not enter into the plan or amend the plan during a Prohibited Period; the trading plan does not permit the Director or Employee to exercise any influence or discretion over how, when, or whether to undertake Dealings.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The only sanctioned way to obtain scheduled liquidity outside a window is a cleared non-discretionary sale plan, which is the realistic alternative to offer in place of a collar.

summary: A funded collar is not possible for any Stockland director or executive, and this is one of the clearest prohibitions in the market. Section 5.3(a) states that Employees, a term that expressly includes non-executive Directors as well as the Managing Director and Senior Executives, must not Deal in Derivatives over Securities at any time, and Derivatives is defined by economic effect as any option, hedge, derivative or like instrument which limits exposure to the market price of Securities, now or in the future, so both collar legs are banned regardless of vesting state, venue or settlement method. Section 5.3(b) independently bans any margin lending arrangement and the creation or giving of a mortgage, security or other right to a lender or financier over any Securities, with only Security Interests existing before the Policy's approval grandfathered, so the secured loan leg fails as well. There is no consent route to either prohibition: the Exceptional Circumstances relief is drafted entirely around selling Securities, consent will not be given if there is any possibility the Policy could be breached, and a refusal is final, confidential and unreasoned. The only sanctioned liquidity routes are an outright sale in a six-week Permitted Trading Window, settled before the window closes and subject to the two times and one times Fixed Pay holding floors, or a pre-cleared non-discretionary trading plan.
